title: Cold rebuild: compile a customer's filter safely
summary: Rebuild CompileUserFilter from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: You wrote **CompileUserFilter** in *ReDoS: when a regex takes down production*: a regex built from a pattern you do
not control, made safe with `RegexOptions.NonBacktracking` and a match timeout, returning `null` for patterns it
cannot run. Now write it again from an **empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution.
Why this one: it is the exact code a senior adds the day a product starts accepting regexes from customers, and the
two exceptions it handles are easy to forget. If you get stuck, go back to the lesson and try again tomorrow.

steps.prompt: Warm up. What does this print?
code: var r = new Regex(@"^[a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)*$", RegexOptions.NonBacktracking, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(100));
steps.explain: NonBacktracking and a timeout combine fine. A lookahead is one of the constructs the linear-time engine cannot run, so the constructor throws `NotSupportedException`, which is not an `ArgumentException`: catch both.

steps.title: Rebuild CompileUserFilter cold
prompt: Write `Regex? CompileUserFilter(string pattern)`: build the regex with `RegexOptions.NonBacktracking` and a 100 ms
match timeout; return `null` when the pattern is invalid or uses a construct NonBacktracking does not support.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
